## Scientific question and frozen design

This preregistered reciprocal experiment uses the exact Aspect-1 genomic,
sample, annotation, LD, and block backbone but generates component assignments
globally and effects under the SBayesR-LV log-variance model. The true theta is
`(log(3), log(2), 0)`, exact global component counts are
34,000/500/300/200, and realized h2 is 0.5. R, LV, and RC use identical
Aspect-2 summary statistics and retained block-eigen inputs.

## LV annotation architecture and q recovery

```{r}
knitr::kable(theta, digits = 4)
knitr::kable(q_recovery, digits = 4)
knitr::kable(q_groups, digits = 4)
knitr::kable(q_stability, digits = 4)
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(figure_dir, "theta_forest.png"),
  rel_path = FALSE)
```

Theta recovery and marker-q truth recovery are judged separately. R-hat alone
is not treated as sufficient evidence; ESS, MCSE, and q chain stability remain
primary.

All three theta intervals contain their generating values and their R-hats are
at most 1.011, but the posterior means are shrunk toward zero. The induced q
posterior is highly reproducible across chains (minimum Pearson 0.997 and
minimum Spearman 0.999), yet it does not pass the preregistered truth-recovery
screen: raw-scale Pearson is 0.915, log-scale Pearson is 0.941, and log-scale
RMSE is 0.299. Thus stable sampling is not, by itself, accurate recovery of the
known marker variance architecture.

## SBayesRC under LV truth

```{r}
knitr::kable(alpha, digits = 4)
knitr::kable(rc_induced, digits = 3)
knitr::kable(rc_stability, digits = 4)
knitr::kable(rc_second, digits = 4)
```

There is no generating RC alpha in this scenario. RC is compared with the
known LV architecture only through its induced component priors and the
registered normalized expected prior second-moment score.

RC raw alpha and its induced active-count architecture remain poorly mixed.
The worst alpha R-hat is 1.640, expected active count has R-hat 1.527, and the
minimum cross-chain Pearson correlation of active-prior means is 0.328. Its
normalized prior second-moment score nevertheless tracks the rank pattern of
q truth better than its amplitude (Spearman 0.942; Pearson 0.841).

## PIP, components, beta, and prediction

```{r}
knitr::kable(pip_pairwise, digits = 4)
knitr::kable(component, digits = 3)
knitr::kable(beta_pairwise, digits = 4)
knitr::kable(genomic, digits = 4)
knitr::kable(downstream, digits = 4)
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(figure_dir, "pip_pairwise.png"),
  rel_path = FALSE)
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(figure_dir, "beta_pairwise.png"),
  rel_path = FALSE)
```

LV does not materially improve beta recovery or validation prediction over
ordinary R in this realization (beta-truth Pearson 0.7828 versus 0.7827;
validation genetic-value correlation 0.7831 versus 0.7819). RC is also within
the preregistered 0.01 equivalence margin downstream, although its expected
active count (542) differs markedly from R (987) and LV (992). Architecture
differences therefore attenuate strongly from component/PIP inference to beta
and prediction.

Runtime is descriptive only. No new timing probe or implementation
optimization was performed.

## Registered decision and limitations

```{r}
knitr::kable(decision)
```

Interpretation follows the Outcome A--G rules frozen before truth generation
and fitting. This is one LV-truth realization on one shared backbone and does
not establish general superiority.

The registered evidence supports Outcomes C, E, and F simultaneously: RC
matches LV within the downstream equivalence margin; ordinary R is essentially
as accurate as LV; and plausible theta intervals coexist with failure of the q
truth-recovery screen. Outcome A is not supported. The post-result decision
addendum changes only the compact emitter from exclusive to nonexclusive
reporting; it does not change a threshold, fit, or scientific design.
